s: I am Maya, and I am here with my friend Lena.
Today we are talking about feelings and character, and how the people around us can make us feel delighted, disappointed, confused, or even surprised.
Yes, today is all about emotions.
We all know the feeling when something makes us delighted.
And we all know the feeling when something leaves us disappointed.
So let us talk about real life, real people, and real feelings.
Let me start with a small story.
Last week, my elderly neighbor, Mrs.
She is eighty-four years old, and she is one of the kindest people I know.
I was delighted to see her garden full of flowers.
She told me about her life, and I felt so happy just to sit with her.
Elderly people often have the best stories.
My grandmother is elderly too, and when I visit her, I always feel delighted because she cooks my favorite food and tells me funny stories from her childhood.
Kind people have a wonderful effect on our mood.
Green had a happy effect on my whole week.
The effect of a kind smile can last for days.

Not every story has a happy ending.
Last month, I bought a ticket for a concert, and I was really excited.
But the singer was sick, and the concert was cancelled.
I waited for weeks, and then nothing happened.
When you expect something wonderful and it does not happen, you feel disappointed.
It is the opposite of delighted.
One day you are delighted, the next day you are disappointed.
That is life, and we all learn to live with it.
And sometimes we feel confused too.
Let me tell you about my friend Tom.
Tom is a good man, but he is sometimes confused by new technology.
Last week, he tried to buy a train ticket on his phone, and he was completely confused.
He pressed the wrong buttons, and the app asked him strange questions.
In the end, he was so confused that he asked a stranger for help.
I think we have all been confused by a new app or a new machine.
I was confused when I first tried to use the ticket machine at the station.
The screen had too many buttons, and I did not know which one to press.
I felt confused and a little embarrassed, but a kind woman helped me.
The important thing is to ask for help and keep trying.
And you know what has a big effect on our feelings?
A kind word can have a wonderful effect on your day.
A rude word can have a bad effect too.
One small action can change everything.
The effect of a smile is amazing.
If you smile at a stranger, the effect is often a smile back.
And if you are honest with people, the effect is trust.
People trust you, and that trust makes life easier for everyone.
Speaking of honesty, let us talk about the word dishonest.
A dishonest person is not truthful.
For example, it was dishonest of my old classmate to copy my homework and say it was his own work.
That was dishonest, and our teacher was very unhappy with him.
When someone is dishonest with you, you feel disappointed and confused at the same time.
You ask yourself, why did they lie?
It is a strange feeling, and it can have a long effect on a friendship.
Honesty is always the better choice.
And we all have things we dislike.
My main dislike is crowded places.
I dislike waiting in long lines, and I dislike loud music in small shops.
What is your biggest dislike, Lena?
My biggest dislike is cold winter mornings!
I dislike winter mornings when my car will not start.
But you know, a dislike is just a feeling.
We can learn to live with the things we dislike, and we can focus on the things we love instead.

Install Muse English and keep learning with us every day!
So, let us remember our seven words today.
Confused means you cannot understand or think clearly.
Delighted means very pleased and happy.
Disappointed means sad because something was not as good as you expected.
Dislike is a feeling of not liking something.
Effect is a change that happens because of something.
And elderly is a kind word for old people.
Think about an elderly person you know, and tell them something kind today.
Do not feel disappointed if your English is not perfect yet.
Never feel confused and give up.
Just keep listening, keep speaking, and stay delighted about your progress.
See you tomorrow on Muse English!
Keep learning, keep smiling, and we will see you tomorrow!
